issues.failure_explanation: The claim says modules over a commutative unital ring are free, directly contradicting the paper's earlier correct observation that modules need not have a basis. Only the particular coordinate modules later used, such as \(\KM^m\), are established to be free.

failure_location.quote: if we define them as a commutative ring with a unit, then we are almost as good in the sense that modules are free modules

issues.title: Commutative unital rings do not make all modules free

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The ring $\KM$ is said to be {\em fully real} or {\em real-like} if its realness is equal to $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The admissible realness values are \(0,2,\ldots,n\) when \(n\) is even and \(1,3,\ldots,n\) when \(n\) is odd. Their number is therefore \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\), not \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) for even \(n\). In particular, at \(n=2\) the source itself exhibits both the complex-number field and the fully real split-complex tubal ring.

failure_location.quote: Since complex rows in $\matM$ come in pairs, the parity of the realness must be equal to the parity of $n$, thus there are, up to isomorphism, $\lceil \nicefrac{n}{2} \rceil$ tubal rings.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the count by \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\), with the admissible realness values listed by parity.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed classification count omits one isomorphism type in every positive even dimension.
issues.title: The number of realness classes is miscounted for even dimension
issues.why_classification: This is a local finite-count correction that does not alter the classification construction or later theory.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition \(a\ne b\) does not ensure that \(a^2-b^2\ne0\): for nonzero elements with \(b=-a\), the first displayed formula divides by zero, while the second branch covers only \(b=a\). Such elements do have weak inverses, but require the missing branch \([a,-a]^T\mapsto[1/(4a),-1/(4a)]^T\).

issues.title: The split-complex weak-inverse formula omits one null-cone branch

Independently chosen SVDs of those slices need not have conjugate-paired singular-vector factors, especially when singular values are repeated. Without enforcing that compatibility, inverse transformation of \(\hat{\tenU}\) and \(\hat{\tenV}\) need not be real, so the proof has not constructed tensors in the asserted spaces \(\KM^{m\times m}\) and \(\KM^{p\times p}\).

failure_location.quote: Construct a SVD decomposition for each frontal slices on its own, collecting the left and right unitary matrices to form \(\hat{\tenU}\) and \(\hat{\tenV}\) respectively, and the singular values in \(\hat{\tenS}\).

issues.title: The t-SVD proof does not ensure that transformed factors return to real tensors

diagnostic_evidence.quote: every row of $\matM$ is either real, or obtained by entry-wise complex conjugation of exactly one other row of $\matM$.

issues.failure_explanation: For real tensors, transformed slices corresponding to conjugate rows of \(\matM\) must themselves be conjugate and hence have equal ranks. The theorem allows different values \(r_j\) on a conjugate pair and truncates the two slices independently. The resulting transformed array then generally lacks conjugate symmetry and has no real inverse transform, so \(\lrapprox{\tenA}{\vr}\) is not a tensor in the stated real tubal algebra. The omitted proof cannot be the same slice-by-slice argument as before because the feasible real slices are coupled.

failure_location.quote: For any \(n\)-size tuple of non-negative integers \(\vr\) such that \(\vr \leq \Mmultirank(\tenA)\), we define the tensor \(\lrapprox{\tenA}{\vr}\) as the tensor in which the frontal domain \(j\) in the transformed space is the \(r_j\) truncated SVD of the \(j\)th frontal face of the transformed \(\tenA\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict \(\vr\) to have equal entries on every conjugate pair and choose conjugate-compatible truncations, or reformulate the optimization for arbitrary bounds by coupling each pair at the smaller permitted rank and recompute the error formula.
issues.overall_effect: The construction, optimality statement, and exact-error expression are unreliable for multirank tuples that are asymmetric on conjugate slice pairs.
issues.title: Arbitrary multirank truncations violate conjugate-pair constraints
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a genuine coupled-slice feasibility argument and modification of either the advertised parameter regime or the stated optimizer and error formula, but not new global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If we are dealing with a tubal ring Algorithm~\ref{alg:find-M} will find $\matM$.
The use of complex numbers is unavoidable. It can be shown that no such real \(\matM\) exists.

issues.failure_explanation: If the sampled element has repeated eigenvalues, an arbitrary eigenbasis of its representation matrix need not be a common eigenbasis for all representation matrices. For example, choosing the unit element gives \(\matR_\vx=I\), whose eigendecomposition can use any basis; subsequent columns then need not produce a transform diagonalizing the product. No sampling distribution, genericity condition, retry, or verification step is provided. The output contract also incorrectly requires a real \(\matM\), although the paper's complex-number example proves that some tubal rings admit no such real transform.
